source_refs.source_text:
### `runReport(options)`

Run a custom GA4 report with arbitrary dimensions and metrics.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options.dimensions` | `string[]` | required | GA4 dimension names |
| `options.metrics` | `string[]` | required | GA4 metric names |
| `options.dateRange` | `string \| DateRange` | `"30d"` | Date range |
| `options.filters` | `Record<string, string>` | `undefined` | Dimension filters |
| `options.orderBy` | `string[]` | `undefined` | Sort order |
| `options.limit` | `number` | `undefined` | Row limit |
| `options.save` | `boolean` | `true` | Save results to JSON |

**Returns:** `Promise<ReportResponse>` — Rows with dimension and metric values.

input_necessity_topics.observed: runReport destructures filters and orderBy, but its request includes only property, dateRanges, dimensions, metrics and a truthy limit. Neither filters nor orderBy contributes to the request or returned response.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Check whether the generated facts preserve the actual unused reads and whether semantic review reports the conflict with the documented filter/sort options. Do not invent filtering/sorting or silently substitute a corrected request.

input_necessity_topics.topic: Date values, defaults and object pass-through
input_necessity_topics.observed: Absent/falsy ranges read the settings default. Object ranges are returned unchanged; shorthand strings select matched day counts, otherwise a 30-day default. Search Console computes ISO dates from separate current-Date values.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Keep control/existence relations and actual object pass-through. Do not remove extra object fields from forward facts merely because an interface contract later needs only startDate/endDate; do not merge distinct clock observations.

input_necessity_topics.topic: Report dimensions, metrics, limits and whole responses
input_necessity_topics.observed: GA4 maps dimension and metric name arrays into request objects. Search Console preserves dimensions, rowLimit and startRow in requestBody. Standard/realtime report functions return their whole response; search analytics selects response.data.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Verify ordered member scopes, optional/truthy controls and actual response selection. Interface necessity must be justified independently of observing these actual arguments.

input_necessity_topics.topic: URL normalization, membership and empty-input early return
input_necessity_topics.observed: URL normalization trims each string and prefixes a missing slash without removing trailing slashes. A nonempty URL list becomes a case-insensitive pagePath inListFilter. The empty normalized list returns rows=[]/rowCount=0 before client access, remote request or save.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Preserve per-member values/order and cardinality/existence controls; an empty-output branch must not fabricate a request or persistence event. Keep requested metrics, dateRange and save controls distinct.

input_necessity_topics.topic: Different metadata outputs have different field needs
input_necessity_topics.observed: getAvailableDimensions selects response.dimensions (default []); getAvailableMetrics selects response.metrics; getPropertyMetadata returns/saves the whole response. getAvailableFields logs dimensions/metrics counts and returns the whole metadata object.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Check output-specific value/presence/cardinality demand and retain full acquisition facts. A selected metadata field does not establish that the remote acquisition supports field projection.

input_necessity_topics.topic: Index notification actions and conditional fallback values
input_necessity_topics.observed: Publish requests send the URL with URL_UPDATED or URL_DELETED. Returned url and notifyTime use response metadata with original-URL/current-time fallbacks. Saving is separately guarded by save.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Keep publish side effects even when no response field is demanded. Preserve request/response pairing, notification type and fallback controls; response-only analysis must not delete an action-required URL.

input_necessity_topics.topic: URL inspection field projection and conditional nested objects
input_necessity_topics.observed: inspectUrl requests inspectionUrl/siteUrl and explicitly constructs indexStatus, optional mobileUsability, optional richResults and inspectionResultLink from response.data.inspectionResult. checkIndexStatus invokes inspectUrl with save:false and stores only URL, verdict-derived indexed, and the full indexStatus object; catch stores an error status.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Verify exact field paths, default/presence conditions, URL-result member pairing and the distinction between standalone inspectUrl obligations and this narrower caller. Do not declare fields globally deletable from one consumer alone.

input_necessity_topics.topic: Sequential batches, per-item outcomes and suppressed inner saves
input_necessity_topics.observed: requestIndexingBatch processes members sequentially and passes save:false to each request. reindexUrls and checkIndexStatus have per-item try/catch, preserve URL/outcome pairing, log URLs, and save one collected batch. requestIndexingBatch itself has no per-item catch.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Keep duplicate/member occurrence identities and different error control behavior. Preserve false inner save flags and required outer writes; console URL observations remain actual uses.

input_necessity_topics.topic: Aggregate results, nested default saves and date-pair identity
input_necessity_topics.observed: High-level workflows collect named subresults and persist the aggregate; many nested report helpers retain their default save:true. compareDateRanges pairs range1 with period1 and range2 with period2, then saves both; it performs no arithmetic comparison.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Retain each real nested/aggregate save and period pairing. Task/source evidence must determine necessity rather than treating all similar writes as duplicates. Do not invent trend calculations in compareDateRanges.

input_necessity_topics.topic: Persistence content and path depend on different inputs
input_necessity_topics.observed: saveResult writes the whole data argument wrapped with savedAt/category/operation/propertyId and optional extraInfo. The path uses resultsDir/category plus a timestamp and sanitized operation/extraInfo. Directory creation is conditional. The written timestamp and filename timestamp are generated separately.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Distinguish content fields, directory/path controls, optional metadata and separate clocks. Preserve the real propertyId metadata even for non-GA4 categories; do not treat an unused returned filepath as an absent storage side effect.

input_necessity_topics.observed: loadResult checks existence then reads/parses, returning null on catch. listResults filters .json, joins paths, sorts descending by filename and optionally slices. getLatestResult optionally uses a sanitized operation substring, chooses the first file, then loads it.

source_refs.source_text:
## Workflow Pattern

Every analysis follows three phases:

### 1. Analyze
Run API functions. Each call hits the Google APIs and returns structured data.

### 2. Auto-Save
All results automatically save as timestamped JSON files to `results/{category}/`. File naming pattern: `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS__operation__extra_info.json`

### 3. Summarize
After analysis, read the saved JSON files and create a markdown summary in `results/summaries/` with data tables, trends, and recommendations.

## Tips

1. **Specify date ranges** — "last 7 days" or "last 90 days" gives different insights than the default 30 days
2. **Request summaries** — After pulling data, ask for a markdown summary with tables and insights
3. **Compare periods** — Use `compareDateRanges()` to spot trends (this month vs last month)
4. **Check real-time data** — `liveSnapshot()` shows who's on the site right now
5. **Combine GA4 + Search Console** — Traffic data plus search query data gives the full picture

input_necessity_topics.observed: The workflow declares analysis, auto-save and reading saved JSON to create Markdown summaries containing tables, trends and recommendations under results/summaries. Tips separately suggest asking for a summary after pulling data.
input_necessity_topics.audit_question: Audit source modality and summary read/write obligations separately from TypeScript call-site counts. No summary implementation appears among the explicit API/saveResult call sites.

## Setup

Install dependencies:

```bash
cd scripts && npm install
```

Configure credentials by creating a `.env` file in the project root:

```
GA4_PROPERTY_ID=123456789
GA4_CLIENT_EMAIL=service-account@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
GA4_PRIVATE_KEY="-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
SEARCH_CONSOLE_SITE_URL=https://your-domain.com
GA4_DEFAULT_DATE_RANGE=30d
```

**Prerequisites**: A Google Cloud project with the Analytics Data API, Search Console API, and Indexing API enabled. A service account with access to your GA4 property and Search Console.

## Quick Start

| User says | Function to call |
|-----------|-----------------|
| "Show me site traffic for the last 30 days" | `siteOverview("30d")` |
| "What are my top search queries?" | `searchConsoleOverview("30d")` |
| "Who's on the site right now?" | `liveSnapshot()` |
| "Reindex these URLs" | `reindexUrls(["https://example.com/page1", ...])` |
| "Compare this month vs last month" | `compareDateRanges({startDate: "30daysAgo", endDate: "today"}, {startDate: "60daysAgo", endDate: "31daysAgo"})` |
| "What pages get the most traffic?" | `contentPerformance("30d")` |

Execute functions by importing from `scripts/src/index.ts`:

```typescript
import { siteOverview, searchConsoleOverview } from './scripts/src/index.js';

const overview = await siteOverview('30d');
```

Or run directly with tsx:

```bash
npx tsx scripts/src/index.ts

#!/bin/bash
cd "$(dirname "$0")" && npm install

// Print help when run directly
if (process.argv[1] === new URL(import.meta.url).pathname) {
  console.log(`
GA4 Analytics Toolkit
=====================

GA4 High-level functions:
  - siteOverview(dateRange?)        Comprehensive site snapshot
  - trafficAnalysis(dateRange?)     Deep dive on sources
  - contentPerformance(dateRange?)  Top pages analysis
  - userBehavior(dateRange?)        Engagement patterns
  - compareDateRanges(range1, range2)  Period comparison
  - liveSnapshot()                  Real-time data

Search Console functions:
  - searchConsoleOverview(dateRange?)  Combined SEO snapshot
  - keywordAnalysis(dateRange?)        Query/keyword analysis
  - seoPagePerformance(dateRange?)     Page-level SEO metrics
  - getTopQueries(dateRange?)          Top search queries
  - getTopPages(dateRange?)            Top pages by clicks
  - getDevicePerformance(dateRange?)   Mobile vs desktop
  - getCountryPerformance(dateRange?)  Traffic by country

Indexing functions:
  - reindexUrls(urls)                  Request re-indexing for URLs
  - checkIndexStatus(urls)             Check if URLs are indexed
  - requestIndexing(url)               Request single URL re-crawl
  - inspectUrl(url)                    Inspect URL index status

Low-level GA4 functions:
  - runReport({ dimensions, metrics, dateRange })
  - getPageViews(dateRange?)
  - getTrafficSources(dateRange?)
  - getUserDemographics(dateRange?)
  - getEventCounts(dateRange?)
  - getActiveUsers()
  - getRealtimeEvents()
  - getPropertyMetadata()

All results are automatically saved to /results directory.
`);
}
